title: Copilot Studio: share agents with other makers on the Microsoft Copilot harness
summary: The roadmap facts, sharing controls and PowerShell example are supported. The briefing correctly distinguishes the roadmap's permissions from Learn's sharing experience; one minor clarification should also acknowledge Learn's separate definition of Viewer as chat-only access.

claims.claim: Agents can be shared with security groups.
claims.quote: All members within security groups that you specify

claims.claim: Only share with individuals (no security groups) restricts sharing to security groups where the rule applies.
claims.quote: If this setting is selected, owners and editors can only share with individuals as viewers. They can't share with a security group. This control doesn't affect an owner's or editor's ability to share with individuals as editors.

claims.claim: Learn warns that external-service connections can be tied to each individual agent user's identity.
claims.quote: Sharing Copilot Studio agents that have connections to external services such as Azure Databricks Genie can be challenging because connections are tied to the identity of each individual agent user.

claims.claim: An agent might work for its maker but not for other users because of those connections.
claims.quote: This means an agent might work for you but not for other users.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; rationale: risk
claims.claim: When an agent tool uses maker credentials, other users can perform operations with the permissions associated with those credentials.
claims.quote: When an agent uses such a connection, other users of the agent can perform operations by using the permissions associated with the maker's credentials.

claims.claim: Connections configured for end-user credentials use each user's own connection at runtime.
claims.quote: Connections configured to use end-user credentials aren't subject to this connection-sharing restriction because each user authenticates by using their own connection at runtime.

claims.claim: Editor permissions can be granted only to individual users, not security groups.
claims.quote: Editor permissions can only be given to individual users. You can't grant Editor permissions to security groups.

claims.claim: No approval step specifically for an Editor's configuration and publication changes is documented in the material found.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot sharing approval Editor; agents-experience publish approval editor. Opened sharing and sharing-controls pages. Results described organization-catalog submission approval, not approval of individual Editor changes; no such change-approval step found.
